source: Copernicus Open Access / Open Geotechnical Infrastructure Archive
geographic_region: Rhine-Ruhr Rail Corridor, Germany (51.4556° N, 7.0116° E)
temporal_resolution: Irregular (12 to 48 days due to decorrelation dropouts)
processing_method: Multi-looked DInSAR without persistent scatterer filtering
known_limitations: Heavy vegetation and scrub growth causes severe volume scattering decorrelation
Interferometric phase is dominated by phase noise; coherence drops below 0.35

independent_reference.reference_source: Rail Track Recording Geometry Vehicle (EM100) Survey
independent_reference.reference_limitations: Track geometry survey measures rails, whereas satellite pixel covers rail slope and vegetation
independent_reference.documented_behavior: Track geometry is stable (< 2 mm ballast variation); satellite InSAR observations are uninterpretable due to severe decorrelation and noise
independent_reference.expected_strata_behavior: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE or LOW_QUALITY suppression; system refuses to manufacture structural risk from noise
